item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 9 September 2026
item.description:
Syp mulls grinding in Octopath Traveler, eyes Final Fantasy Resonance, and wonders why trying something new feels harder than it used to.

Marc makes the case for B.O.B., a rough-but-worthwhile Gray Matter oddity whose highs almost outweigh the cheap deaths and clunky reputation.

Scopique contrasts Ultima Online’s hometown pull with Star Citizen’s planet tech, arguing big worlds need local reasons to keep players grounded.

Wilhelm marks 20 years in EVE Online by crunching ISK and assets, basically a veteran’s check-in on not being “space poor.”

The Friendly Necromancer and Dylan learn Raft the hard way, from starvation and shark hats to finally understanding shark bait and island diving.

Tobold ports old EverQuest instincts into Star Wars Zero Company, using taunts and a jetpack Mandalorian to make kiting surprisingly effective.

Joel’s weeknotes cover cutting YouTube, cleaning feeds, Bandcamp Friday pickups, and a grab bag of reading, podcasts, Silksong, and UFO 50.

Ramen Junkie celebrates Star Trek’s 60th by ranking personal favorites, with DS9, TNG, the TOS movies, and Lower Decks getting the love.

Tim Bray makes the Autistici/Inventati takedown painfully concrete through Emily’s site and email vanishing, with basically no real defense available.

Jeff tests OpenNMC, an open-source APC UPS management card replacement with NUT support that looks a lot friendlier than a $500 NMC3.

Mike digs into classic Mac resources and shows how to embed a custom bitmap font in a HyperCard stack.

Cristian argues Arch Linux’s scary reputation is mostly psychological, with archinstall, docs, and careful updates making it less intimidating than advertised.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 8 September 2026
item.description:
Stargrace’s WoW gold week was mostly smaller transmog sales, some delves and crafting, and the looming question of Blizzard’s 5-million-gold mount.

Aywren makes the case that FFXIV Frontlines is less scary than it sounds, with easy rewards, low pressure, and beginner-friendly quirks.

CrazyKinux shares an EVE Online hauling scare, and how one predictable station warp turned a routine low-sec milk run into a tense lesson.

Nimgimli’s still hooked on The Planet Crafter, where jet boots, a rover, and rockets finally make terraforming feel faster and more dramatic.

Bhagpuss wanders through recent gaming thoughts, screenshot habits, and the sheer UI overload of Black Desert Online in a deliberately loose ramble.

Joar’s August recap admits the tracker lied, but Vancouver downtime still meant WoW, a little Guild Wars 2, and finally finishing Blaugust.

Michael says Aerial_Knight’s MrFreezy is a stylish, satisfying puzzle game, even if late-game power-up choices and hidden level gimmicks get fiddly.

Anarchae rounds up a properly miscellaneous links post, from Blaugust and chronic illness to Yukon cheetahs, airports, COVID, and Linux IPTV.

Dávid serves a cozy photo post with first-time apple pie, sugar-free baking, pogácsa, and a nice nod after yesterday’s blogroll feature.

Warner puts Sunday Morning Reading on hiatus for a happier reason this week: celebrating his grandson’s fifth birthday.

Wilhelm looks back on Star Trek’s 60th with memories of tiny black-and-white TVs and why the show’s color production helped it endure.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 7 September 2026
item.description:
Kimimi finds Kisou Shinden Gen-kaiser delightfully packed with ’90s anime-mecha clichés, with brisk, restrictive design that feels more cozy than limiting.

Margot’s week is all about cozy co-op, handheld tinkering, Big Walk puzzling with Luna, and sampling indie picks like Wanderstop.

Tan’s back-to-school week mixes classroom reshuffling, a busted RGB30 mod, more Terranigma, and RetroArch audio woes on the Pocket Reform.

Blockade85 hits that familiar post-finish slump after Final Fantasy VII and Doom: The Dark Ages, with a backlog ready but nothing feeling right.

Kelly finally fixes a Fedora MariaDB startup bug, tracing it to systemd-tmpfiles choking because the root directory had the wrong ownership.

Brennan takes stock of his digital garden, arguing for more maintenance, optimism, and fewer shiny new seedlings across his corner of the internet.

UltrViolet clocks Google Maps swapping out its old navigation voice for a younger, AI-sounding one with plenty of vocal fry.

Jamie Zawinski shares another gloriously glitched billboard photo, the kind of urban tech failure that looks weirdly like source code.

Bruce Schneier points to car camouflage meant to evade Flock cameras—maybe impractical, but definitely a striking bit of surveillance counterplay.

Dave Winer says Claude is equal parts helpful and maddening while he ports Frontier, great at spotting failures but constantly breaking things too.

Roger runs through his reading habits, from horror and ghost stories to ideal armchair ambience, and makes the case for reading in any form.

Juhis talks blogging as a long-running counterweight to video, plus how software notes, reviews, and deeper reading-driven ideas turn into posts.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 6 September 2026
item.description:
Syp happily defends overleveling in LOTRO, enjoying breezy Bree-land questing while also building a strong Octopath Traveler party.

Tipa power-levels a Paladin/Monk/Enchanter in EverQuest Legends to finish the Fiery Avenger setup before Kunark epic quests arrive.

Shintar digs into SWTOR PTS ops testing, where tweaking a new boss is neat, but blind veteran-mode progression sounds gloriously chaotic.

Azuriel finds 7 Days to Die’s Undead Legacy overhaul slows crafting so much that it accidentally pushes the game further into loot-first play.

David’s Gunderholfen crew recruits fresh magic users and pushes deeper into undead dwarf territory while Grimoire sits this dungeon run out.

Wilhelm runs through likely BlizzCon 2026 reveals, from WoW Midnight and The Last Titan to Classic dates and more Season of Discovery-style experiments.

Tobold argues Star Wars Zero Company leans on one-and-done scripted set pieces, while XCOM 2’s randomness gives it far better replay value.

Emily writes a heartfelt tribute to Peter Cullen, reflecting on Optimus Prime’s impact and a treasured meeting at TFCon.

JJM revisits ZX Spectrum tape loading with the kids, complete with volume fiddling, fake cassettes, and the timeless problem of too many games.

Aneesh shares a brief poem about poetry holding words in form until they finally leap from someone’s lips.

Krikket recaps a big Blaugust 2026 with nearly 180 participants, lots of first-timers, and the full spread of posting awards.

The Friendly Necromancer looks back on finishing Blaugust, mixing EverQuest Legends, D&D, dev logs, and some honest doubts about what the posting sprint accomplished.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 5 September 2026
item.description:
Tipa is intrigued by Final Fantasy Resonance bringing back FFBE’s combo-heavy theorycrafting while ditching the wallet-devouring gacha that killed the original.

Bhagpuss goes sightseeing around Hethereau, trying to figure out whether its long-teased off-limits district is actually changing or just looking prettier.

Welsh Troll wonders how long is too long for Star Citizen and Squadron 42, especially when crowdfunding freedom starts to look directionless.

Shintar is more than ready for BlizzCon to finally say something concrete about WoW Classic, Camelot, and whatever retail announces next.

Marc digs Battle Pinball, a weird 1994 3DO import where two players battle simultaneously on character-themed tables instead of just chasing scores.

Ellie says Blasphemous II’s free Third Sin expansion is a short, gorgeous Castlevania-flavored detour with a new castle, enemies, and a whip.

Wilhelm treats EverQuest Legends like a nostalgia road trip, leaving Blackburrow at 14 for the long old-school run toward Freeport and beyond.

Jimmy spins a funny Porsche story—complete with an accidental Cayenne rental—before turning to Need for Speed: Porsche Unleashed and car-culture history.

Anarchae’s weekly digest mixes job-search stress with Kindaichi reading, P5 Tactica, Fate/GO, Traitors, and the struggle not to overextend themself.

Cristian tosses out a tiny, open-ended question about why so many people like the color blue, then lets the comments run with it.

Jeff restomods a 1995 TrueTime box into a Raspberry Pi stratum 1 NTP server, with GNSS, Chrony, and just enough cautionary Telstra energy.

WCRobinson wraps Blaugust by admitting weekly posting was a stretch, but says the push helped them write faster and finally ship reviews.
